description: Independent ground-truth labels for the PolicyGuard benchmark corpus. Each expected entry is the SME's judgment of a genuine misconfiguration a knowledgeable cloud-security reviewer would flag, decided by reading the .tf BEFORE running PolicyGuard. Precision/recall are measured by comparing PolicyGuard's findings to these labels, scoped to core_policies. Findings for policies outside core_policies are ignored (not counted as FP) so the number reflects the unambiguous core-security set, not opinionated style/tagging checks.

s3_partial_secure.tf.note: Encryption and logging are correctly configured inline; only the public ACL is a real finding. Tests that the secured dimensions are not over-reported.

out_of_scope_clean.tf.note: SNS/SQS/CloudWatch resources in reasonable configs. No core-policy finding expected; out-of-scope tagging/DLQ findings are ignored by the core scope.

s3_split_resource_secure.tf.note: Correctly secured via split resources (aws_s3_bucket_server_side_encryption_configuration / aws_s3_bucket_logging). The S3 policies now recognize these siblings, so zero findings are expected. Kept as a true negative guarding against regressing the split-resource fix.

ec2_bare_insecure.tf.note: IMDSv1-by-default is insecure and should be flagged. PolicyGuard's != "required" check misses the absent-block case, so this is expected to surface as a false negative until the policy handles absence.

azure_secure.tf.note: Securely configured Azure resources, including the azurerm v4 attribute name, reliance on Azure secure defaults, and a multi-rule NSG with admin access restricted to a CIDR. Zero findings expected.
